title.analysis: Authentic title "The Biggest Wealth Killers in Your 20s and 30s (AVOID At All Costs)" is a list-warning frame with an age target. The script delivers six named killers (lifestyle creep, cars, card debt and BNPL, waiting, no emergency fund, looking rich and overtrading) through the Maya/Dylan roommate story, so the promise is honoured; the count is not stated in the title.

script.opening_words: In 2010, Maya and Dylan were roommates, splitting $800 rent on an apartment with an avocado green refrigerator and a dishwasher that only ran if you slammed it twice. They'd graduated that spring from the same program and both started their first real jobs at 52,000 a year. Financially, you couldn't have told them apart. Fast forward 15 years. Maya just took a job she actually wanted for less money without flinching. Dylan is standing in a service center parking
script.ending_words: time. You're going to spend your 20s and 30s. script.analysis: Full 16321 canonical characters read. A single-narrator list explainer built on two composite roommates (Maya and Dylan, same $52,000 start in 2010): hook (Dylan in a parking lot paying for a transmission), reframe that 22-40 dollars are the most powerful, then six killers: lifestyle creep (savings rate, $10,000 raise), cars (payments, depreciation, negative equity, $470 difference), card debt and BNPL, waiting ($500 from 25 vs 35), employer match and median balances, no emergency fund, a school-community promotion, then looking rich and overtrading (behaviour gap), a recap and the truck callback. Arithmetic largely reproduces; the saving-rate figure is stale and several survey figures are unsourced. The stored ending is truncated.
beat_map: Hook: Maya and Dylan, 2010 to 15 years later.
Disclaimer; 20s and 30s are not the warm-up.
Killer 1: lifestyle creep; savings rate; $10,000 raise.
Killer 2: cars; payments, depreciation, negative equity; $470 difference.
Killer 4: waiting; $500 from 25 vs 35; employer match; median balances.
Killer 6: looking rich and overtrading; behaviour gap.
